gpt.text:
From this handoff, you have a stable **Current Champion** (`baseline/champion_v5_latest.json`) and no pending PASS/INCONCLUSIVE candidates. The “Next Commands” are effectively a full autopilot cycle plus a follow-up “what to fix next” report.

### What to do next (recommended order)
Run the three commands exactly in the order shown:

```bash
python3 experiment_system/tools/aub_autopilot.py --registry experiment_system/config/module_registry.yaml --run --select-best
python3 experiment_system/tools/system_autopilot.py --spec experiment_system/config/system_candidates.yaml --run
python3 experiment_system/tools/aub_next_fix.py --registry experiment_system/config/module_registry.yaml --output baseline/reports/next_fix.md
```

### What each command is for
1) **`aub_autopilot.py ... --select-best`**  
   - Runs module-level experiments defined by `module_registry.yaml`.
   - Selects the best-performing candidate module(s) and promotes them (typically updating whatever pointer/artifact your tooling uses for “best”).
   - This is the step most directly competing against your current champion numbers (tuning/lockbox).

2) **`system_autopilot.py ... --run`**  
   - Runs end-to-end system candidates defined in `system_candidates.yaml`.
   - This validates whether module improvements actually translate to system-level gains (and catches integration regressions).

3) **`aub_next_fix.py ... --output ...`**  
   - Generates a human-readable prioritized “next fixes” report at:
     `baseline/reports/next_fix.md`
   - Use this after the runs so it can incorporate the newest results.

### Quick sanity checks after running
- Confirm whether a new champion file/artifact was produced (or whether the tool updated `baseline/champion_v5_latest.json` / a pointer to it).
- Look for:
  - Any regressions where **min** got worse even if **mean** improved (min often indicates worst-case behavior).
  - Discrepancies between module-level wins and system-level results (common sign of coupling/integration issues).

If you paste the stdout summaries (or the resulting report paths / key metrics), I can help interpret whether the newly selected “best” is genuinely better than the current champion and what `next_fix.md` is recommending.
